name: multi_factor_composite_v1
author: quant_system
thesis: Individual indicators are noisy. Combining multiple orthogonal signals — VWAP deviation, RSI, relative volume, index alignment, and VIX regime — into a composite score improves signal quality by diversifying across information sources. The inefficiency exists because most traders use 1-2 indicators and don't systematically combine signals with proper weighting. Not fully arbitraged because the specific combination and weights are unique to this implementation, and the composite approach is harder to reverse-engineer.

conditions: at least 3 of 5 sub-signals are negative
long.confirmation: composite_score must be < -1.5 for 3 consecutive bars

conditions: at least 3 of 5 sub-signals are positive
short.confirmation: composite_score must be > 1.5 for 3 consecutive bars

entry.entry_price: market on third confirmation bar close

exit.trailing_stop: move SL to breakeven after composite_score crosses ±0.5

filters.vix_filter: included in composite score — no separate filter
filters.time_filter: no trades first 30 min or last 30 min
other_filters: require at least 3 of 5 sub-signals to agree (consensus check)

edge.edge_decay_risk: low — diversified across signal types, harder to crowdedly compete with

weaknesses: The weights (0.30, 0.20, etc.) are arbitrary initial guesses. Without proper optimization (which risks overfitting), the composite may not be better than individual signals.
More parameters = more overfitting risk. 5 sub-signals * 2 params each = 10+ tunable parameters. This is at the edge of overfitting territory.
Composite signals are opaque — when the strategy loses, it's hard to diagnose which component failed. Debugging is harder than single-indicator strategies.
Signal correlation: if VWAP deviation and RSI are both capturing the same mean-reversion tendency, the 'diversification' is illusory.
prior_art: Multi-factor model. Standard in quant equity (Barra, Axioma). See: Finding Alphas (Kakushadze), Advances in Financial ML (de Prado) on feature combination.
notes: Use PCA or factor analysis to verify that sub-signals are actually orthogonal. If correlation > 0.5 between any two, merge or drop one. Walk-forward optimization of weights monthly with 6-month lookback.
